units.text: Begin with ENA on the left. Enhanced networking uses hardware-assisted virtualization to improve throughput, packet rate and CPU efficiency on supported instances. Verify the driver and the actual instance limits.

Compare EFA on the right. It supports low-latency communication between nodes for compatible Linux HPC and machine-learning workloads. The application uses a supported software stack, including the appropriate libfabric integration.

Inspect the prerequisites below. EFA needs supported instances, compatible software, same-Zone placement and the required security-group rules. Adding the adapter alone does not accelerate arbitrary applications.

With the full slide restored, separate historical examples from current limits. Older networking options and bandwidth figures are not universal caps. Measure the application's bandwidth, packet rate and latency using the selected instance and software stack.

Start with the job. Tightly coupled HPC tasks exchange data frequently, while independent tasks can scale differently. Elastic capacity can shorten time to results only when the workload can use that capacity effectively.

Look at the workload examples. Genomics, chemistry, financial risk, weather modeling and machine learning have different communication and data-access patterns. Choose the architecture from those patterns rather than the HPC label.

Move to the compute and storage layer. Match CPU or GPU capacity, placement and networking to the job. Select object, shared-file, block or disposable scratch storage according to how the application reads and writes data.

Follow data staging. Direct Connect provides a dedicated network path; encryption must still meet the requirement. DataSync manages supported online transfers. Stage inputs before scaling a large compute fleet that would otherwise wait for data.

Inspect orchestration and recovery. AWS Batch schedules jobs, while ParallelCluster helps manage clusters. Plan checkpoints, persistent results and restart behavior so that replacing capacity does not mean restarting all useful work.

With the complete slide restored, note the offline-transfer boundary. Snowball Edge has been restricted to existing customers since November seventh, twenty twenty-five. Verify eligibility and current alternatives; fast compute cannot compensate for slow data staging or storage.

Start with the capacity range. Minimum, desired and maximum define how an Auto Scaling group manages capacity. Desired capacity is the target the group tries to reach, not proof that healthy instances already exist.

Move to Availability Zones and the launch template. Use supported subnets and a reproducible launch template. The workload must be able to start successfully in the selected locations and serve traffic after initialization.

Inspect the constraints. Capacity shortages, quotas, launch errors and dependency limits can prevent new instances from becoming healthy. Diagnose actual scaling activities and application health rather than assuming the desired number was achieved.

With the original slide visible, follow replacement and zone failure. Auto Scaling can replace instances, but the application must preserve required state and tolerate losing a Zone. Test the full recovery path, including dependencies and replacement capacity.
